edition.check: Level 5: barcode 4047179677011 matches this edition in Discogs (discogs:release/5671084, exact barcode) and the back-cover image confirms BB114 and barcode, but MusicBrainz has no entry with this barcode (search returned 0 for barcode; MB sibling has 4047179677028, different format CD). Only one database carries the barcode, so >=2 independent sources with the barcode is NOT MET. Level 4: barcode match in only one source (Discogs) - MET in the sense of a barcode match in one source. Other editions: MB 1992 CD (718750375322) and 2004 CD (no barcode) have different track counts (11), so competing editions with different tracklists exist, but the input's barcode and vinyl format rule them out - these are different formats/barcodes. Level 4 conditions met, Level 5 not met.
edition.summary: Exact barcode match in Discogs plus a back-cover image consistent with BB114 and the vinyl format, but no second database entry carries this barcode, so it stops at level 4.

tracklist.check: Level 5: two independent sources of the same edition (Discogs vinyl and back-cover image) agree on count, order and titles except for B2 'Tier im Regen' vs 'Tiere im Regen' - a single-word spelling variant. Count 13 and order agree in all three. MET except the spelling variant, which is acceptable at level 5 as a spelling variant. However, the back cover read is a 600px image and was described as possibly truncated; the image confirms titles as read by the vision tool, which itself is a single read. Level 5 requires two independent sources agreeing; Discogs and image agree on 13 tracks and order, with one variant. The MB source is a CD sibling, not the same edition, so it is not an independent source of the same edition. Thus only Discogs+image of same edition: 2 sources, with a spelling deviation. Level 4: one complete source confirmed by a second except for small explained deviations (spelling) - MET.
tracklist.summary: Discogs and back-cover image agree on 13 tracks and order with only the B2 spelling variant, but the second source is the image read by a vision model and the MB data is from the CD sibling, so level 4 applies.

sources.check: Level 5: database plus independent primary source of the same edition - the back-cover image is a photo of the printed cover (primary-like) and Discogs is a database. However the image was obtained via a Discogs-hosted URL, and the vision tool reading is secondary; the image is hosted on the same Discogs entry, so not fully independent. Level 4: two independent database entries (Discogs vinyl and MB CD sibling, differing barcodes) or database + specialised collector site - MB entry is a different edition (CD), so it is not the same edition. Level 3: one good database (Discogs) with a cover image hosted on the same database entry - MET.
sources.summary: Only the Discogs database entry and a cover image hosted on the same Discogs entry cover the vinyl edition; the MusicBrainz entry is a different CD edition, so level 3 applies.
